tema: Participle Clauses — Walking, Having Taken, Fascinated by...

cast_dialogue.linea: Participle clauses compress time, heroes: two actions, one elegant sentence. 'Walking through the old town, Ben noticed a forgotten studio.'
Opening the door carefully, I found hundreds of portraits covered in dust. Fascinated by the faces, I asked the owner about them.
Having taken photographs for sixty years, the old man knew every family in the neighbourhood.
Touched by the story, Ben offered to exhibit the portraits. Not knowing what to say, the old man simply smiled.
Facing the camera once more, the neighbours smiled as in 1960. Being photographed by a friend is the warmest feeling, mis héroes.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Participle clauses join actions sharing the same subject: present participle (Walking...) for simultaneous actions, past participle (Fascinated by...) for passive meaning, perfect participle (Having taken...) for earlier actions. The implied subject MUST match the main clause's subject.

'Having taken' refers to an action after the main clause.
